beta_new: Jam the hand-sized crack in the corner, stepping onto several shelves en route to a piece left in place, where you hang the rope and descend.

The opening crack is wide and sits above a little roof; traverse leftward into a second crack. Follow it through pods onto a shelf holding a clump of small trees, then go up again to bigger trees for the descent.
A bouldery opening move comes first; after that, balance your way up to the anchors.
Squirm up the narrowing chimney, then use some creative contortions to get onto the face. You can finish on the wall or stay inside the crack, and come down on the chains.
Some freedom is allowed: here and there you may pass either side of the bolts. Expect two cruxes, with jugs turning up exactly when you need them.

A corner capped by a roof high above its base starts the line: crank outward to a jam on the lip and pull into the corner, which leads to a stance beneath a bigger roof. Return right toward that roof to place protection, surmount it, and round the lip onto a belay terrace. Natural gear on the face above takes you to the rim.

A short chimney leads onto a belay shelf under a big roof; work out across the roof, regain the face, and follow the crack up to a second belay. A short leftward face then a crack bring you rightward again onto a terrace, and a brief slot finishes the route.
The crack system runs through several roofs and then up a vertical face; a big terrace finishes it, where you rappel from a tree.
Stick-clip the lowest bolt and aid onward under the roof to begin this slopey route.

Leap to a ledge shaped like a U to begin, then pull a stiff mantel and follow the technical wall to a roomy ledge. Rest, then power up the finger-width crack to a further shelf, and finish up a dihedral to the anchors.
Locate a groove at the base for your start, follow it, then straddle the rounded edge to the summit of the pinnacle.
Boulder through the first moves, then stay with the crack, which runs from finger size to hand size, to where it ends; continue past chickenheads to reach the anchors.
Layback the wide crack alongside its bolts; near the second clip, veer left over a string of sidepulls and underclings, then pull through a last bulge to the chains.
A boulder problem gets you to the lowest bolt, then moderate terrain leads easily to the chains.
Easy moves lead up the left-leaning line to the fourth bolt, where a stopper-style crux waits; past it the handholds improve but the feet stay poor all the way to the chains.
Follow the bolts up the corner, work through the heavily plated section, then carry on over the roof and past the pebbly bulge to the cold shuts.
Start as for Nicorette. At the third bolt, step right and slant upward toward the final bolt of Minimum Creep, finishing at its chains.
Climb the face, then cut hard to the left and get onto the arete, following the bolts to the chains. Reach matters here, and shorter climbers may find it harder.
Reach the alcove under the overhang by climbing the neighbouring route, then rock up onto the arete and fight your way along it, making awkward clips. Hanging the draws ahead of time helps.
A squat, blocky roof begins the route; above it a pocketed face leads to the chains over a shallow trough.
Climb the short flake, then step onto big plates and knobs, drifting leftward until you find a good rest. From there the edges shrink, so crimp harder all the way to the chains.
Technical face climbing on solid crimps leads straight up to the anchors; stay on the bolted face and avoid the dirty crack beside it.
The crack system changes character as you go, opening as an offwidth and narrowing to hand size. Finish at the shared anchors, or continue out the roof to the cliff top.
Work leftward to get over the roof, protecting it with a sling around a block and horizontal placements. Continue up the wide crack, then step left to finish at the neighbouring route's anchors.
Climb the face, mixing natural gear placements with the lone bolt for protection.

The lower part is a grubby, moderate crack from offwidth to fist size that runs up to a shelf just short of the top. Above, an overhanging fist crack takes the final twenty feet, and a short chimney completes the route.
Duck beneath the overhang to the start, then pull through the steep pockets; the angle relaxes above and the ground gets more moderate up to the anchor.
Pump your way through the bulge on enormous holds, finishing at a chain anchor.
Edge up past the lower bolts, where a tricky clip or two can arise, to a small roof near the top. Call it a day at the first chains, or keep going for several more bolts of ordinary climbing.
Delicate, intricate footwork is the key to success on this shady slab, which ends at cold-shut anchors.

Climb to the first bolt and fight your way up to a crack that arches right and ends at a ledge. Clip the next bolt and haul over the roof, then take the crack beyond it to a second stance with anchors.
Start on a ledge with a difficult, sharp opening, then ascend a vertical face on gleaming hangers, crossing a brief pocketed stretch on the way to the chains.

Begin on the lower finger crack off to the side, then boulder rightward to rejoin the main crack. Stay with it as it widens and flares out, and when it finishes, smear over the easy slab above, where gear is scarce, to reach the chains.

Angle upward over the face into a fist-size crack splitting a roof, then follow the crack system across several ledges to a comfortable belay ledge below a large roof. Move out the roof with shaky jams and poor footholds, reaching chain anchors past the lip.
Begin from an enormous hueco and ascend the face, aiming for a wide crack. Follow the crack as it flares and then peters out, place gear in a pocket, and carry on across the slab to a rappel tree.
An easy flake angling right leads across to a lone bolt before the large hueco. Inside the cave you stem, jam and use face holds to exit, then exposed stemming leads to the anchors.
Pull through the overhang, then cruise the wall above, finishing on the chain anchors.
Pull an overhang to enter a strange corner, then step out of it leftward and follow the steep wall up to the chains for a surprising finish.
Start from the top of a big boulder and power through the opening, then head left across horizontals and continue via pockets, finishing at the anchors.
The opening is the hard part: either boulder up to the crack, or clip the first bolt of the bolted route above with a stick and use it as an alternative way into the crack.
